papers.title: Smooth Piecewise Cutting for Neural Operator to Handle Discontinuities and Sharp Transitions
papers.abstract: Neural operators have achieved strong performance in learning solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their inherently continuous representations struggle to capture discontinuities and sharp transitions. Existing approaches typically approximate such features within continuous function spaces, often requiring increased model capacity and high-resolution data. In this work, we propose Cut-DeepONet, a two-stage training framework that explicitly models discontinuities while reducing learning complexity. Our approach reformulates the problem via a lifting strategy, partitioning the domain into smooth subregions while representing discontinuities as boundaries in a higher-dimensional space. This separation aligns the operator learning task with the inductive bias of neural networks and avoids directly approximating discontinuities. An additional network predicts input-dependent discontinuity locations for unseen inputs, which are then used to guide the neural operator in generating smooth components within each region. Experiments on benchmark PDEs show that Cut-DeepONet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, even when trained on low-resolution datasets. The method excels on problems with discontinuities and sharp transitions, while using fewer trainable parameters. Our results highlight the benefits of changing the representation of operator learning rather than increasing model complexity.

papers.title: Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces
papers.abstract: This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nystr\"om discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fr\'echet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. The interface is reconstructed by regularized Gauss--Newton iteration in a Fourier space that is progressively enriched as the frequency increases. Numerical experiments assess direct-solver accuracy and reconstruction performance for different interfaces, material configurations, and noise levels.

papers.title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a mass-lumped finite element method for the Allen-Cahn equation that incorporates nonlinear mobility which may degenerate. The spatial approximation uses continuous, piecewise linear, mass-lumped finite elements, while convex splitting is employed for the double-well potential in time. Under the standard non-obtuse mesh condition, it is shown that the resulting fully discrete method preserves the maximum-bound principle unconditionally: if the initial approximation takes values in $[-1, 1]$, then so does the numerical solution at every time level. Additionally, the method dissipates the original discrete Ginzburg-Landau energy without any time-step restriction, even when the mobility vanishes at pure phases. This analysis relies on the monotonicity of the lumped finite element operator and the convexity of the split potential. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties and demonstrate the robustness of the method in phase-separation dynamics involving degenerate mobility.

papers.title: DeepRitzSplit: A Variational Neural Operator Framework for Gradient Flows with Application to Dendritic Growth
papers.abstract: Phase-field models are widely used to simulate microstructure evolution but their numerical solution remains computationally demanding. Neural operator surrogates provide a promising alternative, yet existing approaches are data-driven, requiring large datasets and exhibiting limited robustness when extrapolating to unseen configurations. We introduce DeepRitzSplit, an unsupervised neural operator framework for gradient-flow systems based on a variational formulation of energy-stable splitting schemes. It learns the time evolution semigroup associated with a convex-concave free-energy decomposition by minimizing the underlying variational problem at each time step. It is designed to inherit the dissipative structure of the underlying gradient flow without requiring trajectory datasets. We further introduce a Reaction-Diffusion Neural Operator (RDNO) architecture motivated by splitting schemes, with separate reaction and diffusion components to improve training efficiency and interpretability. We assess the approach on the Allen-Cahn equation and apply it to a phase-field model of anisotropic dendritic growth during solidification. In the Allen-Cahn benchmark, DeepRitzSplit shows better generalization than the supervised baseline on the out-of-distribution configurations tested, using 180 training configurations. In dendritic growth, the method captures the overall phase morphology and dendrite tip velocity well, while the tip radius is more sensitive to the training strategy. Refinement based on the residual of the splitting scheme markedly improves this second-order morphological quantity. The trained operators retain good predictive capabilities on configurations substantially different from the training set. These results demonstrate the potential of variationally trained neural operators as physically informed surrogates for accelerated microstructure simulations.

papers.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
papers.abstract: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

papers.title: Nonzero solutions for Dirichlet problems with the competing (p,q)-Laplacian
papers.abstract: The following equation is considered: $$-\Delta_p u(\boldsymbol{x}) + \Delta_q u(\boldsymbol{x}) = f\big(\boldsymbol{x}, u(\boldsymbol{x})\big)\text{ for } \boldsymbol{x} \in \Omega, \qquad u(\boldsymbol{x}) = 0 \text{ for } \boldsymbol{x}\in \partial \Omega.$$ We start by showing that the energy functional associated with the considered problem no longer has the properties typical of its non-competing counterpart, which prevents a direct application of standard variational and monotonicity methods. Using Ekeland's variational principle combined with properties imposed on the nonlinear term~$f$, we prove the existence of a nonzero generalized solution to the problem. It is also shown that in the one-dimensional case $\Omega = (-1,1)$, assuming that $f$ satisfies the symmetry conditions $$f(x,u) = f(-x,u) = -f(x,-u),$$ together with the sign condition $f(x,u) \geq 0$ for $u \geq 0$ and an appropriate growth bound on $f$, a convex relaxation of the action functional yields the existence of a positive weak solution. Furthermore, we prove that in this setting, and under a slightly stronger sign condition $$f(x,u) > 0\text{ for }u > 0,$$ all global minimizers of the action functional do not vanish in $(-1,1)$ but fail to be of class $C^1$.

papers.title: Regularity of elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure
papers.abstract: We study autonomous elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure of the form \[ -\operatorname{div}\big(\mathfrak a(|Du|)Du\big)=0 \quad \text{in }\ \Omega\subset \mathbb R^n \] Under two-sided quantitative $(p,q)$-growth conditions on $\mathfrak a$, we prove gradient H\"older continuity with constants and exponent depending only on the dimensions, $p$ and $q$. This improves the classical theory initiated by Uhlenbeck by removing the continuity requirement on $\mathfrak a'$. The proof uses nonlinear comparison systems whose regularity follows from a scalar uniformly elliptic equation. Under weaker $(p,q)$-growth conditions on the convex function $\varphi(t):=\int_0^t s\mathfrak a(s)\,ds$, we obtain local $W^{1,s}$-regularity for every $s>1$, and hence H\"older continuity of solutions with every exponent less than one. An additional lower growth condition on $\mathfrak a$ yields local Lipschitz continuity, even when $\mathfrak a$ is discontinuous.

papers.title: Blow-Up and Life-Span for Nonlinear Hardy-H\'enon Parabolic Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the nonlinear Hardy-H\'enon parabolic equation $ u_t=\Delta u+|x|^l|u|^\alpha u,$ $t>0,$ $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$ or $x\in\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}$, with $N\ge1$, $l>-\min\{2,N\}$, $\alpha>0$, with nonnegative initial datum $u_0$. We first establish new criteria for finite-time blow-up. We then derive optimal upper bounds for the life-span $T_{\max}(\lambda\varphi)$ of solutions arising from the initial datum $u_0=\lambda\varphi$. These estimates establish a precise dependence of $T_{\max}(\lambda\varphi)$ on both the initial profile $\varphi$ and the parameter $\lambda$ in the small and large-amplitude regimes.

papers.title: Non-conical classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated singularity
papers.abstract: Several examples of one-homogeneous classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated free boundary singularity are known. Adapting the approach of Caffarelli, Hardt, and Simon for minimal surfaces, we construct non-conical classical solutions with an isolated free boundary singularity by perturbing a one-homogeneous solution $U$. Moreover, if $U$ is strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate), then any solution sufficiently close to $U$ is also strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate).

papers.title: Regularity of Weak Solutions near Singular Minimizing Cones for the One-Phase Free Boundary Problem
papers.abstract: Alt and Caffarelli proved an Allard-type $\epsilon$-regularity theorem near the flat one-homogeneous minimizer of the one-phase free boundary problem. A natural follow-up question is whether an analogous regularity result holds near singular minimizing cones. In this paper, we prove such an $\epsilon$-regularity theorem near a strongly integrable one-phase minimizing cone with an isolated singularity. More precisely, we show that, after a suitable translation and rotation, the free boundary of any non-degenerate weak solution sufficiently close to the cone is graphical over the free boundary of a leaf of the De Silva--Jerison--Shahgholian foliation. This result is analogous to recent $\epsilon$-regularity theorems in minimal surface theory by Edelen and by Edelen--Spolaor; our proof adapts the strategy of Edelen to the one-phase setting.

papers.title: Global regularity of the two-dimensional fractional Boussinesq equations with critical dissipation
papers.abstract: In the present paper, our primary focus is on the Boussinesq equations with fractional velocity dissipation $\Lambda^\alpha u$ and temperature diffusion $\Lambda^\beta\theta$. On the critical balance line $\alpha+\beta=1$, establishing global regularity for weak velocity dissipation has been obstructed by the quadratic convective-buoyancy feedback, and all available results below $\alpha=\frac{10}{13}$ require a smallness assumption on the initial temperature. In this paper, we prove large-data global regularity across the extended regime $\alpha>\frac{\sqrt{57}-5}{4} \approx 0.637$. This provides a step beyond the previous barrier $\alpha=\frac{10}{13}$, unconditionally dismantling the temperature smallness assumption that has persisted in the literature for over a decade. The mathematical mechanism relies on a high-order Quadratic Normal Form transformation $H=\omega-R_{\alpha}\theta-\Bop(\theta,\theta)$ tailored to eliminate non-resonant quadratic vorticity-temperature interactions. Crucially, by uncovering the exact physical scalings of the underlying multilinear commutators and maintaining sharp fractional conjugates in the $L^m$-energy framework, we ensure that the global energy closure is governed entirely by the quadratic thermal dissipation. Once an integrability threshold $m>\frac{2}{\alpha}$ is attained, a fine Littlewood-Paley transport estimate drives a fractional regularity gain $H \in B_{r,\infty}^{3\alpha-2}$, ensuring the velocity field achieves critical drift regularity $C^{\alpha}$. By Silvestre-type drift regularization, this spontaneously generates positive H\"older continuity for the temperature, which in turn elevates the drift regularity strictly beyond the critical threshold, unlocking non-local Schauder estimates to prevent finite-time singularity formation.

papers.title: On nonlocal geometric rigidity estimates in bounded uniform domains
papers.abstract: We prove fractional geometric rigidity estimates and fractional Korn's first inequalities with general singular weights in bounded uniform domains in $\mathbb R^n.$ The classical choice of the energy well $SO(n)$ for the geometric rigidity estimate fails due to the lack of a notion of orientation for Lebesgue fields. The remedy is to choose $O(n)$ as the energy well. Due to the recently developed theory of local-to-nonlocal passage of rigidity estimates developed by the first author, both estimates reduce to the analogous local estimates on the cube, which we prove in several steps by compactness and linearization arguments.

papers.title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-\Delta)^m u=u^{(n+2m)/(n-2m)}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0$. The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $\Delta^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-\Delta u$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.

papers.title: Critical Resonance and the Radial Branch in Maz'ya's Weighted Hessian--Gradient Inequality
papers.abstract: We study the sharp constant $C(p,\gamma)$ in Maz'ya's planar weighted inequality \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|\nabla\psi|^p|x|^{p(\gamma-1)}\, \mathrm{d} x \le C(p,\gamma)\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|D^2\psi|_{\mathrm{F}}^p|x|^{p\gamma}\, \mathrm{d} x, \] where $|\cdot|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. For every fixed $1\le p<\infty$, with $a=\gamma-1+2/p$, we prove \[ C(p,\gamma)^{-1}=2^{p/2}|a|^p+O_p(|a|^{p+1})\qquad(a\to0). \] The leading term comes from the first angular harmonics after the Emden--Fowler transform. We also determine explicit exterior parameter rays on which the unrestricted constant equals the radial value $(1+a^2)^{-p/2}$. The proof uses an entropy identity and a homogeneous calibration. In the remaining transition region, we obtain symmetry-breaking intervals and a necessary and sufficient condition for nonnegativity of the periodic second variation at the radial state. An explicit example shows that global symmetry breaking can occur even when this second variation is nonnegative.

papers.title: Delaunay classification of positive singular solutions to the critical Lane--Emden system
papers.abstract: We classify positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system \begin{align*} \begin{cases} -\Delta u=v^p & ~~\text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\\ -\Delta v=u^q &~~ \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}, \end{cases} \end{align*} with a nonremovable singularity at $0$ (i.e., $\lim_{x\to0}u(x)=\lim_{x\to0}v(x)=+\infty$), where $n\ge3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy \[ \frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}=\frac{n-2}{n}. \] Without additional growth or integrability assumptions, we establish radial symmetry about the origin, strict radial decrease, and global two-sided power bounds for both components. Furthermore, every such solution can be written as \[ u(x)=|x|^{-\alpha}U(\log|x|),\qquad v(x)=|x|^{-\beta}V(\log|x|), \] where $\alpha=\frac{n}{q+1}$, $\beta=\frac{n}{p+1}$, and $(U,V)$ is either the positive equilibrium $(A,B)=((\frac{\alpha}{\beta})^{\frac{\alpha}{2}}, (\frac{\alpha}{\beta})^{\frac{\beta}{2}})$ or a positive nonconstant periodic solution of the associated Emden--Fowler system. These periodic solutions form a Delaunay family: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,A)$, there is a unique profile pair, up to translation in $t=\log|x|$, with $\min_{\mathbb{R}}U=\varepsilon$. The Hamiltonian energy provides an alternative parameter, decreasing continuously and strictly from zero to the equilibrium energy as $\varepsilon$ increases from $0$ to $A$. The common least period of the two components tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and to the period of the linearized oscillation at $(A,B)$ as $\varepsilon\uparrow A$. The classification includes the case of a sublinear exponent.

papers.title: Complete uniqueness for two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows
papers.abstract: Alt, Caffarelli and Friedman established the existence of two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows in [Asymmetric jet flows. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35, 29--68, 1982]. In their formulation, the constant fluid speed $\lambda$ on the free boundaries and the downstream asymptotic angle $\theta$ are selected as part of the solution. In this paper, we prove that the asymmetric jet is unique for a prescribed nozzle and mass flux. We first establish the strict vertical monotonicity of the stream function $u$ and introduce the partial hodograph coordinates $\xi=x$ and $\eta=u(x,y)$, which map every fluid domain onto the same fixed strip. Under this framework, each jet is characterized by a height function $y=h(\xi,\eta)$, which determines the vertical position along the streamline $u=\eta$ at horizontal coordinate $\xi$. By analyzing the difference between the height functions of two candidate jets on this strip, we derive an elliptic equation with Dirichlet conditions on the fixed walls and conormal conditions on the free boundaries. Combining these mixed boundary conditions with the asymptotic behaviors, we first establish the uniqueness of the free-boundary fluid speed $\lambda$. For the resulting common speed, a local perturbation of the height function near a nozzle endpoint, together with the maximum principle, proves that the two height functions must coincide. Inverting the partial hodograph transformation then establishes the uniqueness of the physical jet.

papers.title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: The Reaction-Flux Landscape and Maximizing Sequences
papers.abstract: We continue our study of a PDE-constrained variational model for maximizing the total reaction flux by optimizing the spatial distribution of catalytic materials, such as enzymes. The total amount of enzyme is fixed, and the substrate concentration is governed by a reaction-diffusion equation with prescribed boundary values. We consider both linear and nonlinear Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics. In previous work, we constructed a maximizing sequence, computed the first and second variations of the reaction functional, and established the nonexistence of local maximizers. Here, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis. We prove that the functional is strictly concave for linear kinetics but need not be concave or convex for nonlinear kinetics. We also show that no critical points exist. We then characterize maximizing sequences and identify all their possible limiting measures. Our analysis reveals the mechanism of reaction maximization through spatial localization: maximizing sequences concentrate enzymes near the portion of the boundary where the substrate concentration is largest. Moreover, the landscape of the functional defining the total reaction differs between the linear and nonlinear cases, a point less emphasized in applications. Consistent with existing biophysical studies, these findings motivate the development and analysis of regularized models.

papers.title: On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4\pi$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass \(m<4\pi\), the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for \(m>4\pi\), there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. For the fluid-coupled system, Winkler first established global generalized solvability under the condition \(m<2\pi\) and proposed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2\pi$ and $4\pi$. In the present work, we resolve this open problem and show that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact: every admissible initial datum with total mass \(m<4\pi\) generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded with respect to time. Our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality. The key underlying observation is that combining relative isoperimetric estimates with rearrangement techniques yields a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality on bounded planar domains with an explicit leading constant.

papers.title: Positive self-similar solutions of a parabolic equation with spatially weighted absorption in a half-space
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of $u_t-\Delta u+x_1^{2\alpha}|u|^{q-1}u=0$ in the half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, with $\alpha>-1$ and $q>1$, vanishing on $\{x_1=0\}$ and at $t=0$ away from the origin. Let $q_c=(N+3+2\alpha)/(N+1)$. For $1<q<q_c$ we prove that there is exactly one positive self-similar solution continuous away from the origin, and that its profile satisfies Gaussian bounds that are sharp up to multiplicative constants. For $q\ge q_c$ there is none. We also show that, after removing the Gaussian factor, the profile has an angular limit shape $\Phi$ in every mode, give an integral formula for its Kummer coefficients, prove that $\Phi$ is real-analytic and is the uniform limit of the rescaled profiles, that $\Phi/(\eta_1/|\eta|)$ is monotone along meridians, and that $\Phi$ is proportional to $\eta_1/|\eta|$ if and only if $2\alpha+q=1$. Every self-similar solution of finite energy, or continuous away from the origin, is dominated in absolute value by the positive one, and for $(N+4+2\alpha)/(N+2)\le q<q_c$ the only nontrivial ones are $\pm u_s$. For $\alpha=0$ existence, uniqueness and the upper bound are due to Marcus and V\'eron; the lower bound with the sharp exponent and the description of $\Phi$ are new also in that case. The existence and uniqueness proofs use a Brezis--Oswald type comparison principle and explicit barriers, given by explicit formulas; the analysis of $\Phi$ uses Kummer functions.

papers.title: Dynamics of subcritical threshold solutions for the three-dimensional energy-critical NLS
papers.abstract: We extend the radial threshold classification of Duyckaerts and Merle on the lower kinetic branch to nonradial solutions of the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in \(\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\). At the ground state energy and with initial gradient norm strictly below that of the ground state, every solution is global and either scatters in both time directions or is a symmetry transform of the special solution \(W^-\), possibly after conjugate time reversal. The proof combines Su and Zhao's below-threshold scattering theorem with a coercivity estimate for the interaction form at threshold under a kinetic gap and a local analysis near the ground state orbit.

papers.title: Boundary singularities for the Lane-Emden equation
papers.abstract: For every $n\ge3$ and $(n+1)/(n-1)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct positive solutions of $\Delta u+u^p=0$ in the half-space with zero Dirichlet data away from the origin, the homogeneous singular profile there, and Poisson-kernel decay at infinity, resolving a question of del Pino--Musso--Pacard. Under a weighted non-degeneracy condition, these half-space solutions serve as building blocks for positive very weak solutions in smooth bounded domains, singular along prescribed compact smooth boundary submanifolds of normal dimension $n$. We verify non-degeneracy in the initial stable interval and at and just beyond its threshold when this lies below $(n+2)/(n-2)$. For isolated boundary singularities, the construction applies throughout the strict subcritical interval outside a locally finite exceptional set.

papers.title: Single-scale regularity from Dirichlet energy for the five-dimensional stationary Navier--Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We establish an interior $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion for suitable weak solutions of the unforced stationary Navier--Stokes equations in an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^5$. There exists a universal constant $\varepsilon_\ast>0$ such that $x_0$ is regular if, for some ball $B_R(x_0)\subset\Omega$ with $R>0$, \[ \frac1R\int_{B_R(x_0)}|\nabla u|^2\,dx \leq \varepsilon_\ast^2. \] The main difficulty is that the Dirichlet energy controls the velocity oscillation while its mean may be arbitrarily large. Subtracting the mean introduces a large constant drift into the perturbation equation. Moreover, smallness in $H^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. We overcome these difficulties through uniform Oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. As a consequence, the singular set has zero one-dimensional upper Minkowski content on every compact subset of $\Omega$, and hence local upper Minkowski dimension at most one.

papers.title: Kolmogorov Obstacle Problems: Euclidean Free Boundary Regularity under a Cone Condition
papers.abstract: We study obstacle problems for Kolmogorov-type operators that diffuse in one variable and transport in another. Such problems describe American options on running averages. Under a cone estimate, a strong monotonicity condition on the solution in the diffusive direction, we show that the free boundary is a graph in the diffusive direction with H\"older continuous first derivatives in the Euclidean sense, and that every free boundary point is regular. The key observation is that a Euclidean Lipschitz free boundary is flat at the intrinsic scale. For the American fixed-strike Asian option we verify the cone estimate, so that its exercise boundary has the same regularity.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the critical $p$-Laplace equation near isolated singularities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of weak solutions to the following critical $p$-Laplace equation \[ -\Delta_p u=u^{p^*-1}, \quad u\ge0 \quad\hbox{in }B_1\setminus\{0\}, \] where $\Delta_pu=\diver(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian with $1<p<n$, $p^*=\frac{np}{n-p}$ is the Sobolev critical exponent and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We develop a nonlinear potential-theoretic method to establish sharp upper bounds for solutions, without using the method of moving planes or moving spheres. Furthermore, we use Steiner symmetrization to study the radial symmetry of global singular solutions, and thereby classify all Fowler singular solutions. Finally, we prove that every local singular solution is asymptotic to a global Fowler singular solution.

papers.title: Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
papers.abstract: We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annulus, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.

papers.title: Well-posedness of weak solutions for the time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model
papers.abstract: This paper constructs a time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model describing the interaction between a free fluid and a thermo-poroelastic medium and provides a rigorous mathematical analysis. The model consists of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations and the heat equation in the free-fluid region, together with the thermo-poroelasticity equations in the porous medium. The two regions are coupled on a fixed interface through conditions for normal velocity, tangential velocity, stress balance, temperature continuity, and heat flux continuity. Under a small-data assumption, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a weak solution for this fully dynamic nonlinear coupled system. The proof employs the Galerkin method to construct semi-discrete approximations, establishes uniform a priori estimates that enable the extension of local solutions to global ones, and invokes compactness arguments to pass to the limit, yielding a solution to the original coupled system.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability of planar contact waves for the 3-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space
papers.abstract: We prove the global nonlinear stability of small planar contact waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\R^3$ under general $H^4(\R^3)$ perturbations, without any $L^1$ integrability or zero-mass assumptions. Unlike the one-dimensional problem or the periodic channel, the problem in $\R^3$ admits neither a Poincar\'e inequality in the transverse directions nor a square-integrable anti-derivative. Our proof relies on three main ingredients: a perturbation around the one-dimensional Navier--Stokes solution starting from the smooth contact profile, a formulation of the low-order perturbation system in the velocity, pressure, and entropy variables with separate estimates for the velocity--pressure pair and the entropy, and the construction of characteristic and space-time Gaussian weight functions. Combining these weighted estimates with higher-order derivative bounds and homogeneous Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation yields global stability and algebraic $L^\infty$ decay rates in $\R^3$.

papers.title: Sharper energy scaling bounds of the singularly perturbed Tartar square
papers.abstract: In this article, we discuss the scaling behaviour of the singularly perturbed Tartar square, revisiting the results by [R\"uland-Tribuzio '22]. Therein, it was proven that both lower and upper bounds satisfy a behaviour of the same type, up to a small mismatch of logarithmic powers. We show by an improvement of the ansatz free lower bound that the logarithmic powers indeed match and that the bounds are of order $\exp( - C \log(\varepsilon^{-1})^{1/2} )$ for suitable constants $C = C_{\rm low}$ and $C = C_{\rm upp}$, where $\varepsilon$ denotes the singular perturbation parameter. More specifically, the bootstrap argument in the Fourier space is refined by resorting to Fourier multipliers enjoying $L^\infty$-bounds which are constructed via de la Vall\'ee Poussin kernels. Regarding upper bounds, we perform iterated branching constructions sharpening the upper bound of [Winter '97] which resorted to an iteration of laminates as a competitor. Eventually, the mismatch of upper and lower bound is quantified, and for quadratic energies we obtain the bounds $C_{\rm low} \leq 7.0339$ and $C_{\rm upp} \geq 2 \log(2) - \nu $ for any $\nu>0$.

papers.title: Angular Besov Refinement of the Spherical Stein--Tomas Theorem
papers.abstract: The spherical Stein--Tomas inequality maps $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$ into $L^4(\mathbb R^3)$. We study its refinement in which the angular input is measured by the strictly weaker Besov norm $B^0_{2,4}(\mathbb S^2)$. The central separated-band inequality bounds the squared $L^2$ norm of the product of extensions from degrees $L\ll K$ by $C(L/K)$ times the squared input norms. An exact spherical-Hankel expansion controls the far field, while angular-momentum leakage and transversality handle the Fresnel region. We construct scale-separated, normalized angular bands for which the extension norm is equivalent to the $\ell^4$ norm of the coefficients. This proves that the fourth-power summation is optimal and quantitatively distinguishes the result from the classical $\ell^2$ summation. As an application, small angular Besov data generate small $L^4$ solutions to the cubic nonlinear Helmholtz equation in $\mathbb R^3$, with a smallness condition that remains sharp on multiscale data even when their $L^2$ norm is arbitrarily large or infinite. The associated on-shell nonlinear scattering amplitude has improved angular $B^0_{2,4/3}$ regularity, and its leading cubic term is quantitatively decoupled across widely separated angular bands.

papers.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
papers.abstract: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).
